title: Understanding Bootstrapping
text: Bootstrapping is a resampling method that involves repeatedly drawing samples from a data set and calculating a statistic for each sample. This helps in estimating the sampling distribution of the statistic.

title: Sample Size and Distribution Shape
text: As the sample size increases, the Central Limit Theorem suggests that the sampling distribution of the sample mean will become approximately normal, regardless of the shape of the population distribution.

title: Bootstrapped Sampling Distribution
text: The bootstrapped sampling distribution of a statistic may not always become normal as the sample size increases. It depends on the original data distribution and the statistic being calculated.

title: Evaluating the Statement
text: Consider whether the bootstrapped sampling distribution of a statistic will always become roughly normal as the sample size increases.
